claim_verdicts.evidence: Glossary etcd: "Consistent and highly-available key value store used as Kubernetes' backing store for all cluster data." api-server-bypass-risks: "The only clients that need access are the Kubernetes API server and any backup tooling that you use." configure-upgrade-etcd: "ideally only the API server should have access to it." R2 text now limits the rule to the cluster's components (backup tooling is not one), matching the docs.

kubernetes-api.md: "The core of Kubernetes' control plane is the API server and the HTTP API that it exposes. Users, the different parts of your cluster, and external components all communicate with one another through the API server." control-plane-node-communication.md: "All API usage from nodes (or the pods they run) terminates at the API server."

Glossary kube-scheduler: "Control plane component that watches for newly created Pods with no assigned node, and selects a node for them to run on." kube-scheduler.md: "The scheduler then notifies the API server about this decision in a process called binding." Execution: temp Pod review-tmp-cc showed NODE donhang-worker2 while STATUS ContainerCreating (container started later on the node, not by the scheduler).
claim_verdicts.source: refs/kubernetes-website: reference/glossary/kube-scheduler.md; concepts/scheduling-eviction/kube-scheduler.md; kubectl run in namespace donhang

claim_verdicts.evidence: Glossary kubelet: "An agent that runs on each node in the cluster. It makes sure that containers are running in a Pod." nodes.md: "--node-status-update-frequency - Specifies how often kubelet posts its node status to the API server." pod-lifecycle.md: "the kubelet sets the Pod's condition to ContainersReady". Execution: review-tmp-cc went ContainerCreating -> Running within 2 s as reported via the API server.

Glossary controller: "In Kubernetes, controllers are control loops that watch the state of your cluster, then make or request changes where needed. Each controller tries to move the current cluster state closer to the desired state." controller.md: "a control loop is a non-terminating loop that regulates the state of a system."

Glossary kube-controller-manager: "Control plane component that runs controller processes." controller.md: "Kubernetes comes with a set of built-in controllers that run inside the kube-controller-manager."

Architecture page: "Control plane components are deployed as static Pods, managed by the kubelet on specific nodes. This is a common approach used by tools like kubeadm." R1 execution: /etc/kubernetes/manifests holds etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler yaml; kubelet is a systemd service. R2 `kubectl get pods -A -o wide`: etcd/kube-apiserver RESTARTS 0 AGE 23h, kube-scheduler/kube-controller-manager RESTARTS `5 (23h ago)` AGE 5d22h, so RESTARTS/AGE do vary.

For pods, the node name is included." kubelet-sync-loop.md: "The `kubelet` runs a sync loop that periodically reconciles the desired state (a Pod spec) with the actual state of the running containers"; queues work "for the Pods assigned to its node (where `nodeName` matches the node)". kube-scheduler.md: "A scheduler watches for newly created Pods that have no Node assigned." scheduling-framework.md: unschedulable Pod "will be returned to the queue and retried."
